Happy Thursday. It's **Andrew** and **Swin** again. We're still awaiting some
state results, but we already know that Tuesday night was [one for the history
books](https://zeteo.com/p/republicans-2026-bloodbath-was-way). Republicans
are - yes - in disarray, and Democrats are deservedly rejoicing at the
shocking scale of their victory in the midterms. Conservative politicians know
_exactly_ who's to blame… they just won't say who, for fear of death threats
and lost career opportunities.

In today's '**First Draft** ,' we get into just how much the GOP elite is now
quietly blaming the president of the United States and his American "[Prime
Minister](https://zeteo.com/p/stephen-miller-trump-running-world)" for their
catastrophic 2026 election outcomes. Plus, **Chuck Schumer** says he'll be
Senate Majority Leader again, but progressive voices in his ranks aren't quite
so sure, and there's more news about Trump's catastrophic war. Let's read in.

Following their [election night
](https://zeteo.com/p/republicans-2026-bloodbath-was-
way)**["bloodbath"](https://zeteo.com/p/republicans-2026-bloodbath-was-way)**
Tuesday, a wide array of prominent Republicans on Capitol Hill, within the
Trump-Vance administration, and in the high-roller donor class are now ready
to vent to us about how it is, quite simply, President Donald **" Trump's
fucking fault,"** as one _very_ pissed-off GOP megadonor put it.

Almost all blamed Trump's illegal war on Iran, which most of them never
thought should have been launched. (None blamed so-called "War Secretary" Pete
Hegseth, Trump's leading Iran warmonger whose job is now reportedly in [some
danger](https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/midterm-election-results-2026-latest-
updates/card/trump-asking-allies-about-keeping-hegseth-87O7do9uhfXFXEDgPyA5).)
They all blamed rising costs that their infallible god-emperor Trump helped
jack up, having won in 2024 with his blatantly hollow campaign vows to bring
them down.

But a significant number of these sources also blamed - though they will not
dare do so publicly, either - Stephen Miller, Trump's most important sidekick,
at least when it comes to his domestic policy agenda.

**" He screwed us big time,"** a longtime GOP operative who worked on
competitive 2026 races said of Miller, the president's top policy architect,
his White House deputy chief of staff, and the man who oversees Trump's
federal crackdowns and ethnic-cleansing campaign.

This consultant, along with several other plugged-in national and
battleground-state-based Republican sources, specifically points to the Trump
White House's two years of mass-deportation sprees around the country, which
helped cave in the president's poll numbers (including on immigration, his
signature policy issue) and unleashed a tidal wave of lawlessness, state
violence and terror, racial profiling, and the intimidation efforts against
legal immigrants and U.S. citizens.

In battleground states - including red states that voted for Trump three times
- there has been a large erosion of the president and his party's support
among Hispanic voters, which reached unusually strong levels in 2024. Internal
